//: Reference settings.json — injection & egress hardening (Policy 10/11). Native-first.
//order: Prefer the OS-sandbox egress allowlist over the Bash denylist: it breaks the trifecta egress leg for ALL commands, not just curl/wget. The hooks cover the two gaps native features leave: pipe-to-shell when the sandbox is off, and invisible-char smuggling in fetched content.
//sandbox: sandbox.enabled is REQUIRED — the sandbox is off by default and allowedDomains alone does nothing. strictAllowlist denies any unlisted domain instead of prompting; honored from user, managed, or --settings scope, ignored in project .claude/settings*.json. This is the deterministic egress leg-break — the single strongest control here. credentials.files mode deny hides those paths from sandboxed commands; mode mask needs experimental network.tlsTerminate and degrades to deny on macOS/Windows.
//permissions: Deny wins over allow. WebFetch scoped to an allowlist; fetchers kept off auto-approve as a belt-and-suspenders fallback for when the sandbox is disabled.
//mcp: Lock the set of MCP servers so a poisoned/renamed server can't be silently added. The real lock is the OS-path managed-mcp.json (exclusive control). In managed settings, allowedMcpServers/deniedMcpServers are the lists; allowManagedMcpServersOnly only restricts where the allowlist is read from and is a no-op without a managed allowedMcpServers — set both. Native has NO tool-description drift detection — that's the SessionStart-hash gap noted in enforcement.md.
//managed: In managed (MDM) settings, lock the rules so user/project scopes can't relax them (disableBypassPermissionsMode lives inside permissions, above).
//hooks: Copy both scripts to ~/.claude/hooks/. PreToolUse blocks pipe-to-shell forms globs can't express (fallback when sandbox off). PostToolUse strips invisible-char injection vectors from WebFetch, Read and MCP output — the indirect-injection gap WebFetch context-isolation does NOT cover, and repo files / MCP results get no isolation at all. secret-leak-check.sh pauses the turn when tool output matches a live-credential pattern (secrets.md incident response).
